title.narrative: Provision of integrated humanitarian lifesaving assistance and services to most vulnerable conflict-affected population, including children and women in Myanmar

description.narrative: The project aims to deliver critical humanitarian support to vulnerable populations in temporary sites, host communities, and conflict-affected areas, focusing on lifesaving interventions across multiple sectors. For 25,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs), comprehensive WASH assistance ensures access to clean and sufficient water, the construction of safe, child-friendly, and gender-sensitive latrines, the installation of handwashing facilities, distribution of essential WASH supplies, and hygiene promotion to prevent disease outbreaks. Simultaneously, life-saving nutrition services target 13,500 children under five and 8,100 pregnant and lactating women (PLW) through screening and treatment for acute malnutrition, alongside micronutrient supplementation to address deficiencies such as anemia. The project also includes community-level child protection activities, offering mental health and psychosocial support, case management for survivors of gender-based violence and unaccompanied children, awareness campaigns on violence prevention, explosive ordnance risk education, and capacity building for child protection systems. To support education continuity, the provision of Education in Emergencies (EiE) supplies, including individual learning materials and Essential Learning Package kits, will benefit 12,000 children in Kayin, Sagaing, and Magway, ensuring access to continuous learning opportunities. Additionally, multipurpose cash assistance is provided to crisis-affected families to improve access to education, nutrition, and WASH services, with targeted financial support for unaccompanied children in Shan and Mandalay.
